route: The decision version of the evaluation-query model: how many strategy evaluations decide val(v0) >= 1/2, and what the rank-deficient relaxation is.
object: K(D), the set of harmonic systems on the controlled skeleton consistent with the answers to t evaluation queries, viewed as a PRODUCT OF PER-INCIDENCE CONSISTENCY FIBRES inside the substochastic simplex, together with the two numbers Phi(D) = sup val*(v0) and phi(D) = inf val*(v0) over it.
headline: The relaxation K(D) of the evaluation model is a product of polytopes whose extremal consistent games are (rank+1)-sparse; a single evaluation NEVER decides the bit at a strictly switchable start (explicit self-loop lift raising the value to 1); and a certified adversary shows |C|+1 evaluations are necessary to decide val(v0) >= 1/2 at |C| = 2 and 3, against the |C|+2 of thm:eval-queries for naming — so in this model deciding is not cheaper than naming, contrary to what prop:hdp-eval leaves open.

results.name: ed:fibre -- the consistency fibre, and what an evaluation algorithm may output
results.statement: Fix a controlled skeleton with |C| = m and let Delta = {z = (q,p) >= 0 : q + sum p <= 1}, <x> := (1,x), the reading of z at x being <x>.z. For data D = ((sigma_r, x_r, A_r))_{r<=t} put K_{v,a}(D) := {z in Delta : <x_r>.z = A_r(v,a), r <= t} and rho(D) := dim span{<x_r>}. Then K(D) is exactly the set of STOPPING members of the product of the K_{v,a}(D), and every member reproduces the data exactly (val_{sigma_r}|_C = x_r and the appeals are A_r). Moreover (1) the image of Delta under z |-> (<x_r>.z)_r is conv{0, 1_t, X_u (u in C)} with X_u := (x_r(u))_r, so K_{v,a}(D) is nonempty iff the appeal profile (A_r(v,a))_r lies in that polytope; (2) a nonempty fibre is a polytope of dimension m+1-rho(D) each of whose vertices has at most rho(D)+1 nonzero entries; (3) at rho(D) = m+1 the system is unique. Consequently (ed:decide-criterion) a deterministic evaluation algorithm may output 'val(v0) >= 1/2' only when every member of K(D) satisfies it and 'val(v0) < 1/2' only when every member does, so the evaluation-query complexity of the DECISION problem is exactly the depth of the pursuit game on the pair (Phi, phi).
results.why_not_implied: thm:eval-queries uses only that SOME consistent system exists and that each non-halting answer raises the rank by one; it says nothing about the shape of the consistent set -- that it is a product over incidences, its dimension m+1-rho, the hull criterion for nonemptiness, or the sparsity of its vertices -- and it is a statement about naming, not about which outputs a decision algorithm is entitled to make.
results.argument: Reproduction: at a Max vertex x_r(v) = A_r(v,sigma_r(v)) = <x_r>.z_{v,sigma_r(v)} and at a Min vertex x_r(u) = min_a A_r(u,a), so x_r is a fixed point of the Shapley operator of the member with Max frozen at sigma_r; the member is stopping, so that fixed point is unique (thm:contraction), whence val_{sigma_r}|_C = x_r and the appeals are the readings. (1) Delta is the simplex on the m+2 vertices 0, e_q, e_{p_u}; a linear image of a polytope is the hull of the images of its vertices, which are 0, 1_t, X_u. (2) The fibre is Delta cut by rho independent equations; a vertex needs m+1-rho of the m+2 facets z_i >= 0, sum z <= 1 additionally tight, leaving rho nonzeros if sum z <= 1 is slack and rho+1 if it is tight. (3) rho = m+1 makes each equation system determined. The criterion clause is immediate: the output is a function of the data, and every member produces exactly that data.
results.verification: Implemented in fibre.py (exact rational vertex enumeration with row reduction for the rank) and used throughout. Every enumerated vertex is re-checked against the equalities and against Delta in Fraction arithmetic; the reproduction clause is re-checked from the rows for every world in the certificates (verify_cert.py, 400 nodes at m=3 and 16 at m=2, 4800+ rows). Clause (3) is exercised directly: on 8 random m=3 systems Phi(D) equals the true value at every datum of rank m+1 = 4 (measured_phi_m3.txt).

results.name: ed:vertex -- the extremal consistent games are sparse (with ed:mobius)
results.statement: (One player.) Let val_sigma denote the least fixed point of x |-> q_sigma + P_sigma x. (ed:mobius) If a single row z_{v,sigma(v)} moves along a segment of Delta with all other rows fixed, then det(I - P_sigma) = gamma + delta s and the Cramer numerator = alpha + beta s are affine in the parameter, det(I-P_sigma) >= 0 throughout, and where it is positive val_sigma(v0) = (alpha + beta s)/(gamma + delta s) is a Moebius function with a denominator of constant sign, hence MONOTONE. (ed:vertex) Therefore for every sigma both the supremum and the infimum of val_{M,sigma}(v0) over M in the product of the fibres are attained at systems all of whose rows are VERTICES of their fibres, hence -- by ed:fibre(2) -- have at most rho(D)+1 nonzero entries; so Phi(D) = max_sigma sup_M val_{M,sigma}(v0) is attained at a (rho(D)+1)-SPARSE consistent system. At t = 0 the extremal consistent games are DETERMINISTIC (every action goes to t_0, to t_1, or to a single controlled vertex with probability one), and Phi(empty) = 1, phi(empty) = 0.
results.why_not_implied: thm:transport-objective says the value vector of ONE fixed game is a vertex of that game's transport polytope Q(G); ed:vertex is about a different polytope, the set of GAMES consistent with observed data, and locates the extremisers of a value functional over it, with a sparsity bound in the rank of the data -- nothing about Q(G) bounds the number of nonzero entries of the rows of an extremal consistent system.
results.argument: ed:mobius: only row v of I-P_sigma and entry v of q_sigma depend on the parameter, and each affinely; a determinant is affine in any one row, so numerator and denominator are affine; for substochastic P every eigenvalue lies in the closed unit disc, so det(I-P) = prod (1-lambda_i) >= 0 (real factors 1-lambda >= 0, conjugate pairs |1-lambda|^2); a Moebius function with denominator of constant sign has derivative (beta gamma - alpha delta)/(gamma + delta s)^2 of constant sign. ed:vertex: scale every row by 1-eps, so that every P is strictly substochastic and I-P invertible, and note the scaled system lies in the product of the fibres of the scaled data, whose vertices are the scaled vertices; move blocks to maximising vertices one at a time (each step does not decrease the value by ed:mobius, and later steps do not undo earlier ones); finitely many vertex systems, so one recurs along eps -> 0; and val_{(1-eps)N,sigma} = sum_k (1-eps)^{k+1} P^k q increases to val_{N,sigma} by monotone convergence, giving the limit. At t = 0 the fibres are Delta itself.
results.verification: exact_sup.py computes Phi(D) exactly by enumerating the product of fibre vertices for every target strategy; ascent.py performs the block ascent of the proof. On 8 random nondegenerate stopping m=3 systems and 5 successive data sets each (40 data sets), the block-ascent optimum and the exhaustive product optimum agreed on every one of the 40 values, and at rank m+1 both equalled the true val*(v0) (measured_phi_m3.txt against the ascent table). All arithmetic exact.

results.name: ed:one-query -- one evaluation never decides at a strictly switchable start
results.statement: (One player.) Let M be a stopping harmonic system, sigma_1 a Max strategy, x_1 = val_{M,sigma_1}|_C, D the data of that single query, and let v in C be strictly switchable: A := A_1(v, 1-sigma_1(v)) > xi := x_1(v). Then xi < 1, and replacing the single row z_{v,1-sigma_1(v)} by z' := ((A-xi)/(1-xi), ((1-A)/(1-xi)) e_v) gives a system M' that lies in K(D), is stopping, and has val_{M',sigma_1[v]}(v) = 1. Hence sup{val*_N(v) : N in K(D)} = 1, attained. In particular if the start v0 is itself strictly switchable at sigma_1 and val*_M(v0) < 1/2 then Phi(D) = 1 >= 1/2 > val*_M(v0) >= phi(D): both bits occur in K(D) and no evaluation algorithm decides the bit from that query. If instead sigma_1 is closed, then it is closed in every member of K(D) and one query decides, val* = x_1.
results.why_not_implied: prop:hdp-eval is a lower bound on NAMING an optimal strategy on a family whose members are pairwise isomorphic (so the bit is constant) and degenerate (ties at every masked vertex); it yields no lower bound for the decision problem and none for nondegenerate games. ed:one-query is a statement about every stopping system, with an explicit second consistent game, and it is a bound on deciding the bit.
results.argument: q' := (A-xi)/(1-xi) > 0 and s' := (1-A)/(1-xi) >= 0 satisfy q' + s' = 1, so z' in Delta; its reading at x_1 is q' + s' xi = (A - xi + xi - A xi)/(1-xi) = A, the recorded appeal, so M' lies in the product of fibres; the row changed is not the one sigma_1 uses, so val_{sigma_1} is unchanged and M' reproduces D. M' is stopping because z' has q' > 0, so it is not a full-mass action and every trap of M' is a trap of M. At sigma := sigma_1[v] the row of v is supported on v alone, so val_sigma(v) = q' + s' val_sigma(v), i.e. val_sigma(v) = q'/(1-s') = 1 since 1-s' = (A-xi)/(1-xi) = q'. Closedness is a property of the data alone, so it transfers to every member, where lem:local-global makes sigma_1 optimal.
results.verification: t_onequery.py: over all Max strategies of random dyadic stopping nondegenerate systems, 1520 triples (system, strategy, strictly switchable vertex) at m = 3 (720) and m = 4 (800). In every one of the 1520 the constructed row lies in Delta, the modified system is stopping, it reproduces the value vector AND all four (resp. eight) appeals of the query exactly, and val_{sigma_1[v]}(v) = 1; zero failures. 1504 of the 1520 lifted systems are also nondegenerate (16 acquire a tie). Independently, exact_sup.py returned Phi = 1 at t = 1 on all 8 random m=3 systems of measured_phi_m3.txt.

results.name: ed:amplify -- the level-c lift and its exact obstruction
results.statement: (One player.) Let c in (0,1] and sigma* a Max strategy. For v in C set S^c_v := {z >= 0 : q + c sum p = c, <x_r>.z = A_r(v,sigma*(v)) for r <= t}. Then S^c_v is nonempty iff the appeal profile (A_r(v,sigma*(v)))_r lies in H_c := conv{c 1_t, X_u (u in C)}. If S^c_v is nonempty for every v and rows z'_v can be chosen there so that in the digraph v -> supp(p'_v) every vertex reaches one with q' > 0, then the system M' with those rows replaced lies in K(D), is stopping, and has val_{M',sigma*} identically c on C; hence Phi(D) >= c, and for c >= 1/2 the data does not decide the bit. Equivalently (common-direction form) if d satisfies <x_r>.d = 0 (r <= t) and <c1>.d = 1 -- possible exactly when <c1> is outside span{<x_r>}, hence only while rho(D) <= m -- then z'_v := z_{v,sigma*(v)} + lambda_v d with lambda_v := c - <c1>.z_{v,sigma*(v)} has the required readings automatically and lies in S^c_v as soon as it is nonnegative; the nonnegativity is the whole content and is paid out of the escape masses lambda_v. A nonnegative d exists only if some controlled vertex has value 0 in every recorded query, which lem:switch forbids in a nondegenerate one-player game once that vertex is flipped.
results.why_not_implied: thm:eval-queries' rank argument counts INFORMATIVE answers and never constructs a second consistent game; ed:amplify constructs, from data of rank at most m, an explicit consistent stopping game whose value at a chosen unqueried strategy is a prescribed constant, gives the exact nonemptiness criterion as membership in a hull H_c, and identifies why the construction dies (nonnegativity against the escape masses, and the lem:switch obstruction to a nonnegative direction).
results.argument: {z in Delta : q + c sum p = c} is the hull of c e_q and the e_{p_u} (from q = c(1 - sum p) >= 0 one gets sum p <= 1 and q + sum p = c + (1-c) sum p <= 1), so its image under the readings is conv{c 1_t, X_u}, giving the criterion; the fibre over the profile is S^c_v. Each z'_v has the recorded readings, so M' lies in the product of fibres, and at a vertex where sigma_r agrees with sigma* the recorded appeal is x_r(v), so x_r is still the fixed point at sigma_r and M' reproduces D. A row of M' has full mass in C only if q'_v = 0; the reachability hypothesis makes no such set closed, so M' has no trap and is stopping. At sigma* the frozen matrix has row sums (c - q'_v)/c with q'_v = c(1 - sum p'_v), so (I - P')(c 1) = q', and I - P' is invertible, whence val_{sigma*} = c 1.
results.verification: lift.py (c = 1) and liftc.py (general c) build the lift by exact vertex enumeration of S^c_v; every lift returned is rebuilt as a system and re-checked: stopping, reproduces the value vector and ALL appeals of every recorded query, val_{sigma*} = c on C, val*(v0) >= 1/2, and nondegeneracy flagged. Measured on random dyadic stopping nondegenerate systems: at m = 3 the c = 1 lift exists for t = 1,2,3 on 2 of 8 systems and through t = 2 on 4 more; at m = 4 with rows of mass <= 15/16 through t = 3; the criterion fails exactly when a closed strategy has been queried, as the theorem forces. Phi itself (a weaker requirement than a flat lift) stayed above 1/2 through t = m = 4 on one of six such m = 4 systems and equalled the true value at t = m+1 on all six (measured_phi_m4.txt).

results.name: ed:lower -- |C|+1 evaluations are necessary to decide, at |C| = 2 and 3
results.statement: For m = 2 and m = 3 there is a family of NONDEGENERATE stopping one-player SSGs, all with the same controlled skeleton (m Max vertices, every successor a private average name), containing members with val(v0) >= 1/2 and members with val(v0) < 1/2, on which every deterministic evaluation algorithm needs at least m+1 = |C|+1 evaluations. The family is produced by an adversary that holds a datum D and, for EVERY strategy the algorithm may ask, produces a member W of K(D) that is stopping, nondegenerate, has val*_W(v0) < 1/2, leaves the asked strategy strictly switchable somewhere and records val_{W,sigma}(v0) < 1/2, together with a second member Y of K(D u new) that is stopping, nondegenerate and has val*_Y(v0) >= 1/2; so after m answers both bits are consistent with the data and by ed:decide-criterion no output is legitimate. Since the upper bound is d(G)+2 <= |C|+2 (thm:eval-queries), deciding the bit and naming an optimal strategy have the same evaluation-query complexity to within one query at these sizes.
results.why_not_implied: prop:hdp-eval bounds NAMING on a degenerate family whose bit is constant, and its own statement disclaims any consequence for prob:main and for the nondegenerate class of def:improvement-uso; ed:lower is a bound for the bit itself, on a nondegenerate family whose members lie on both sides of 1/2, and needs an adversary over consistent games rather than a hidden bit-string.
results.argument: Run any deterministic algorithm against the adversary. Each query is answered by the world stored at the corresponding node of the adversary tree; repeated queries return the recorded answer and add nothing. After m answers the data D is that of a node of depth m, and K(D) contains the node's NO world and its YES witness, both reproducing D exactly; the algorithm's output depends on the data alone, so it is wrong on one of the two. Hence at least m+1 queries. The tree is exhaustive: from every node of depth < m EVERY unqueried strategy occurs as a child, so no query sequence escapes it.
results.verification: advcert.py searched and dumped the trees; cert_m2_d2.json (16 nodes = 4 + 12) and cert_m3_d3.json (400 nodes = 8 + 56 + 336). verify_cert.py rechecks each certificate from the rows alone, independently of the search, in exact rational arithmetic: tree completeness (every unqueried strategy present as a child of every node), and for each node the NO world stopping, nondegenerate, val*(v0) < 1/2, the last query strictly switchable, the recorded value at v0 below 1/2, and agreement of its answers with those recorded by ALL its ancestors; and the YES witness stopping, nondegenerate, val*(v0) >= 1/2, and agreeing with the NO worlds on the whole path. Both certificates verify: 'certificate OK: 400 nodes, 400 NO worlds, 400 YES witnesses; depth 3 at m = 3'. The 4800 rows of the m=3 certificate are rational with largest denominator a 280-bit integer, none a unit vector or the zero row, so by ed:rational-row every member is a stopping SSG on at most about 10^4 vertices with the same 3 Max vertices. A depth-4 search at m = 3 was started and CUT SHORT (no root query resolved within ten minutes), so nothing is claimed about tightness.

results.name: ed:rational-row -- rational first-passage rows are cheap
results.statement: Let r_1..r_l >= 0 be rationals with common denominator D >= 1 and sum r_j <= 1, and d := ceil(log_2 D). There is a gadget of at most (l+2)d fresh average vertices with a designated entry such that a token entering reaches the target w_j with probability exactly r_j and t_0 with the remaining probability, meeting no other vertex on the way, and leaves the gadget with probability 1. Hence lem:dyadic-row's conclusion holds for an ARBITRARY rational harmonic system: one whose rows have common denominator D is the normal form of an SSG on |C| + 2 + O(|C|^2 log D) vertices, stopping exactly when the system has no full-mass action set. Moreover prefixing every incidence with one fresh average vertex whose two successors coincide changes no row and no trap, so a family of such systems can be given ONE skeleton carrying no information beyond C and its owners, even when some row is a unit vector or zero.
results.why_not_implied: lem:dyadic-row realises DYADIC rows by a rejection-free binary tree; a row of denominator 3 is not dyadic and is not realised by any acyclic gadget of fair coins, so the extension needs the rejection loop and a fresh termination argument. It matters here because every witness this route produces is a vertex of a consistency fibre, hence rational and essentially never dyadic.
results.argument: Put K_0 = 0, K_j = D(r_1 + ... + r_j), integers with K_l <= D <= 2^d, and take the complete binary tree of depth d with a fair coin at each internal node. Assign leaf i to w_j when K_{j-1} <= i < K_j, to t_0 when K_l <= i < D, and back to the ENTRY when i >= D. One pass reaches a uniform leaf and rejects with probability (2^d - D)/2^d < 1/2; passes are independent, so the gadget is left with probability 1 and the exit is w_j with probability (K_j - K_{j-1})/D = r_j. As in lem:dyadic-row an internal node whose whole leaf interval carries one assignment is deleted and its incoming edge redirected, so only nodes straddling one of the l+2 boundaries K_1..K_l, D survive. A trap cannot meet the gadget unless it contains all targets of a full-mass row, since from every surviving node some leaf of its subtree carries an assignment; so the traps are exactly the full-mass sets of the system.
results.verification: ratrow.py builds the gadget and solves, in exact rational arithmetic, the linear system for the exit probabilities. Nine rows checked, all exact: (1/3,1/3) at D=3 in 3 nodes, (2/7,3/7) at D=7 in 5, (1/5) at D=5 in 5, (4/15,1/3,2/5) at D=15 in 7 (a stochastic row), (1/3,1/3,1/3) at D=3 in 3, (3/8) at D=8 in 3, (11/13) at D=13 in 6, (7/37,9/37,20/37) at D=37 in 11, and the unit row at D=1 in 0; every node count is below the bound (l+2)d.

restatements.label: thm:eval-queries
restatements.note: 'A closed queried strategy settles the bit': closedness is a property of the data, so it holds in every consistent system, where lem:local-global makes the strategy optimal -- this is exactly thm:eval-queries' halting test read for the decision problem, and is not new.

restatements.label: rem:eval-queries
restatements.note: 'At full rank rho = m+1 the consistent system is unique, so computing Phi(D) is prob:main itself' -- rem:eval-queries already records that the relaxation is target-equivalent once the data has full rank; only the low-rank regime is new here.

gap: The general lower bound is NOT proved; only |C| = 2 and |C| = 3 are certified. The missing statement, exactly: 'For every m there is a nondegenerate stopping one-player harmonic system W_0 on m controlled vertices with val*(v0) < 1/2 such that, for every datum D of at most m queries generated by the adversary from W_0, some member of K(D) is stopping and nondegenerate with val*(v0) < 1/2 and leaves the next query strictly switchable, and some member of K(D) is stopping and nondegenerate with val*(v0) >= 1/2.' Two further items are open and flagged as such: whether |C|+1 is tight (the depth-4 search at m = 3 was cut short after ten minutes with no root query resolved, so neither |C|+1 nor |C|+2 is established as the exact complexity at m = 3), and the two-player case (ed:mobius and ed:vertex are proved for one player only -- with a Min vertex val_sigma is a minimum of Moebius functions of one row and the monotonicity argument fails, so the sparsity of the extremal consistent systems is unproved there, while ed:fibre, ed:decide-criterion, ed:amplify's construction and ed:rational-row are player-neutral).
next_steps:
1. Prove the general adversary. ed:amplify(b) says exactly what W_0 must have: dense rows whose escape masses lambda_v are small compared with their entries, so that the perturbation d -- which must have mixed signs, since a nonnegative d needs a controlled vertex of value 0 in every recorded query and lem:switch forbids that once the algorithm flips it -- can be paid for. The concrete sub-problem: bound below the largest c for which a d with <x_r>.d = 0, <c1>.d = 1 and |d_i| <= min_v z_v(i)/lambda_v exists, in terms of the distance from <c1> to span{<x_r>}; the measurements (mass <= 15/16 keeps Phi >= 1/2 to t = m at m = 4; mass <= 3/4 loses it at t = 2 or 3) say the threshold is governed by that ratio.
2. Two players. Redo ed:mobius for a Min vertex: val_sigma is a minimum of Moebius functions of one row, and the right statement is presumably that the SUPREMUM over the fibre product is still attained at block vertices even though the function is not monotone (each Min strategy tau gives a monotone branch). A proof would extend ed:vertex, hence the exact computation of Phi, to the whole model.
3. Tightness at small m. Push the certified adversary to depth |C|+1 (is |C|+2 necessary?) and to m = 4 depth 4. The search is the bottleneck: the current adversary samples the fibre product; replacing that sampling by a direct LP that maximises the switchability slack at the asked strategy subject to val* < 1/2 and to ed:amplify's feasibility would make depth 4 at m = 4 reachable and would also keep the denominators small (they now reach 280 bits after three queries).
4. The randomised question (part (C) of the brief) is untouched: prop:hdp-eval has m/log(m+1) for naming; nothing is known here for the zero-error randomised DECISION complexity, and the adversary tree of ed:lower is the object on which to run the standard distributional argument.
5. Connect to the paper's own families. Every family of the exponential lower bounds (thm:ladder, cor:slack-stalls, thm:wedge-proved, thm:hybrid-lower, thm:cv-lower, thm:bc-lower) is decided by |C|+2 evaluations; computing Phi(D) along their all-switches runs would say after how many rounds their bit becomes forced, which is a sharper form of rem:run-informs than the rank count.
prior_art: From memory, flagged unchecked against the sources. (a) The evaluation-query model with a consistency set is the shape of an inverse-problem / 'inverse reinforcement learning' argument: the set of MDPs consistent with observed policy evaluations, and its per-row polytope description, is the standard object there; I have not seen the sparsity of its extremisers stated. (b) That a linear-fractional function with a denominator of constant sign is quasi-linear, so that its extrema over a polytope sit at vertices, is LP folklore (Charnes-Cooper); frontier.tex already uses it in the proof around thm:bc-cert, over different hexagons. (c) The rejection gadget of ed:rational-row is the Knuth-Yao / von Neumann rejection method for simulating a rational distribution with fair coins; what is new here is only that it is compatible with the trap characterisation lem:trapchar, hence produces a stopping SSG. (d) Adversary arguments over 'all inputs consistent with the answers so far' are the standard decision-tree adversary method. (e) The upper bound side is Condon's and the paper's own thm:eval-queries; no fifth imported fact is used -- every step above is proved from thm:determinacy and the paper's own lemmas.
